chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْه، عَنِ الْيَقْطِينِيِّ، عَنِ يُونُسَ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from al-Yaqtini, from Yunus who said:

chunks.arabic_text: الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: يَا يُونُسُ ارْفُقْ بِهِمْ، فَإِنَّ كَلَامَكَ يُدِقُّ عَلَيْهِمْ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: إِنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ لِي: زَنْدِيقٌ، قَالَ لِي: مَا يُضْرُكَ أَنْ تَكُونَ فِي يَدَيْكَ لُؤْلُؤَةٌ فَيَقُولُ لَكَ النَّاسُ: هِيَ حِصَاةٌ، وَمَا كَانَ يَنْفَعُكَ إِذَا كَانَ فِي يَدِكَ حِصَاةٌ فَيَقُولُ النَّاسُ: هِيَ لُؤْلُؤَةٌ

translations.en: The Righteous Servant (peace be upon him) said: O Yunus, be lenient with them, for your words are hard-hitting on them. I said: But they say to me: 'Zindiq' (atheist/doubter). He said to me: What does it matter to you if you have a pearl in your hands and the people say to you: 'It is a stone'? And what would benefit you if you had a stone in your hand and the people said: 'It is a pearl'?

en.summary: The Righteous Servant (peace be upon him) advises Yunus to be gentle with people because their harsh words can be difficult to bear. He uses the analogy of a pearl versus a stone to illustrate that external perception does not change the intrinsic value or truth of what one possesses, regardless of whether people call a believer a 'Zindiq' or a disbeliever a believer.
en.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith about being lenient with people and the analogy of the pearl and the stone?

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: The Righteous Servant (a title often used for the Imams)
key_terms.زَنْدِيقٌ: Zindiq (a term for a doubter or heretic, often used by opponents)
